**Response:**
When you receive an mRNA vaccine, it's injected into your body. The mRNA in the vaccine contains genetic instructions for making a viral protein, such as the spike protein of SARS-CoV-2. Your cells use this mRNA to produce the viral protein. These proteins are displayed on the cell surface or released into the surrounding area. Your immune system detects these foreign proteins and mounts an immune response by producing antibodies and activating immune cells like B cells and T cells. This prepares your body to fight future infections by the actual virus because your immune system already knows how to respond to the viral proteins. The mRNA is not incorporated into your cell DNA and does not cause a long-term infection because it is temporary and degraded after use.
